description: Client SDK media-path counters, live since the OTel collector's Prometheus exporter and scrape job landed. An empty panel here is AMBIGUOUS - it does not mean zero drops. See the READ FIRST panel for the three-step discriminator before reading any panel. key_custody=operator: the client encrypts; MC holds the meeting KEK and can read; this is not end-to-end and not zero-trust (ADR-0036 §4).

panels.description: Dashboard-level premise notice. Read before any panel below.

options.content:
# AN EMPTY PANEL ON THIS BOARD IS AMBIGUOUS

**This board is live.** The client SDK emits over OTLP-HTTP to the GC telemetry proxy, the OTel collector accumulates and exports, and Prometheus scrapes it. Verified end to end from sdk-core's own built bundle through GC on the cluster - not a synthetic payload.

**That is exactly why empty no longer means one thing.** Before the exporter landed, an empty panel meant the pipeline was unwired and nothing else. Now it is ambiguous between *no drops occurred*, *no browser has been connected recently*, and *the pipeline broke*. **Do not read an empty panel as 'nothing bad happened' until you have discriminated.**

## The three-step discriminator

1. **`up{job="otel-collector"} == 1`** - is the collector being scraped at all? If not, every panel below is meaningless and the problem is the collector or the scrape, not the client.
2. **`count(dt_client_media_frames_received_total)`** - has *any* browser emitted within the collector's `metric_expiration` window? No result means no client has reported recently; it says nothing about drops. **This is the ONLY liveness signal for the client fleet** - there is no per-browser `up` and there structurally cannot be one, because a per-session `service.instance.id` is barred by ADR-0036 §11.
3. **Only if 1 and 2 both hold** does an empty drop panel mean zero drops.

(Step 2 depends on the collector's `metric_expiration`; the value lives in `infra/services/otel-collector/collector.yaml` and its derivation in `docs/observability/alert-conventions.md`. It is deliberately not restated here - a number copied onto a board outlives the config it was copied from.)

## This board's empty-panel meaning is the OPPOSITE of mh-media.json's

**Do not copy wording between the two boards.** On *Media Handler - Media Path*, an empty drop panel means no drops occurred - unambiguously the healthy state, because MH registers its media series eagerly at startup and they exist at zero whether or not anything flows. Here, client series are created lazily on first emission, so absence and zero are different states and only the discriminator above tells them apart. This distinction got *sharper* when the pipeline was fixed, not softer.

## Timestamps are collector-arrival, not browser-event

Delta points are restamped with the collector's clock. Values are correct, but a spike here may be an artefact rather than a burst: session teardown force-flushes pending deltas at one instant, a backgrounded tab flushes on resume, and a collector outage **re-dates** whatever the browsers buffered across it. Full reading guidance: `docs/observability/metrics/client.md` §Stored series shape.

## Key custody

`key_custody=operator`. The client encrypts media; MC holds the per-meeting KEK and can read it; MH, transport and storage cannot. That is accepted operator custody, **not end-to-end and not zero-trust** (ADR-0036 §4).

Triage for the key-material path: `docs/runbooks/mc-incident-response.md` Scenario 16: Missing Key Material.

panels.title: READ FIRST - how to read an empty panel on this board

panels.description: The two ends of the receive-path accounting identity received = accepted + sum(drops by reason), ratified in docs/observability/metrics/client.md. received is counted AT THE WIRE before any parse or verification; accepted is counted after the frame opened. A gap between them that the drop panel does not explain means the identity is broken and one of the three counters has a missing emission site. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Frames Received / Accepted

panels.description: Frames the receive path could not open, by frozen reject reason. THE SIGNAL THIS BOARD EXISTS FOR: the FOUR key-material reasons MCMediaMissingKeyMaterial selects - no_kek_for_generation (KEK generation newer than held - MC's push has not arrived), kek_generation_stale (generation older than this client retains), no_roster_entry (no usable identity key for the sender) and unwrap_failed (an authenticated frame whose KEK unwrap failed: a KEK-bytes split between sender and receiver under one generation, or a sender wrap bug; transit corruption lands on signature_invalid instead, because the signature covers the wrap block) - are, per ADR-0036 §11, the only signal for a join or rotation path that has silently stopped delivering keys. The first three are expected transiently at join and after a KEK rotation, and sustained is the fault; unwrap_failed has NO healthy transient. Split on reason FIRST; the four arms have different remedies (docs/runbooks/mc-incident-response.md Scenario 16) and are not equally instrumented - the conflicting-KEK tripwire panel below is the small-denominator witness for the unwrap_failed split. The alert's ratio, threshold and duration live in the rule (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml) and are not restated here. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS. The export pipeline is LIVE, so empty can mean no drops occurred, no browser has reported within the collector's metric_expiration, or the pipeline broke - run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MH MEDIA-PATH BOARD, where the drop panels read a flat ZERO when healthy (those counters are present-at-zero from startup; an ABSENT series there is a fault). Client series are created lazily on first emission, so here absence and zero are different states; do not carry the MH reading across. No client reject reason is video-gated - every token that can appear on this counter is reachable in this story. Stated explicitly because the equivalent MH drop panels DO name two reasons that cannot fire until video, and silence here would be indistinguishable from having forgotten to check. There is deliberately no 'or vector(0)' in this query: it would fabricate a series and flatten the by-reason breakdown that triage depends on.
panels.title: Receive Path - Frame Drops by Reason

panels.description: Wrapped-key outcomes on frames that were ACCEPTED - neither value ever reaches the drop counter, and counting one as a drop would silently break the receive-path accounting identity. kek_generation_not_held means one key id arrived under a second wrap and the frame played off a cached transmit key. An honest sender of this SDK cannot produce it: on every KEK change it rotates to a NEW key id (R-13), which arrives uncached and lands on the DROP reasons instead. A sustained non-zero rate therefore means a non-conforming or hostile sender that re-wraps rather than rotates, NOT rotation lag. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Non-Dropping Wrapped-Key Outcomes

panels.description: Gap frames and reorder events on the downlink, plus terminal decoder errors. Gaps and reorders are network-shaped; decoder errors are terminal AudioDecoder failures and carry no reason label by design (AudioDecoder provides no bounded vocabulary, and an unbounded one here is the cardinality hazard ADR-0036 §11 exists to prevent). AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Downlink Continuity and Decode

panels.description: Frames arriving on a relay stream_id this client never declared in its ReceiveCapability. The relay region is UNAUTHENTICATED - a handler writes stream_id freely and nobody signs it - so an undeclared value creates no receiver state and is counted here instead; the frame is still verified and attributed from its own key id. A sustained rate means a handler is routing to slots this subscriber did not ask for. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Undeclared Stream IDs

panels.description: Datagrams that left the device on the media datagram path; the denominator for the send-drop ratio. ONE INCREMENT PER TARGET HANDLER PER CAPTURED FRAME, NOT ONE PER FRAME: a sender whose edges span two handlers (ADR-0036 §9) advances this TWICE for one captured frame, so this is not a capture rate and must not be read as one. THE NAME SAYS FRAMES AND THE VALUE COUNTS DATAGRAMS - deliberately, matching dt_client_media_frames_received_total, which has counted datagrams-at-the-wire since story 1. Both ends of the ratio are therefore in the same unit: the send-drop counter is raised inside the per-lane send path, so counting frames here would make one captured frame that succeeded on handler A and was refused on handler B read as 50% loss on a sender that reached A perfectly. MUTE IS NOT VISIBLE HERE AND MUST NOT BE INFERRED FROM IT: while client-muted nothing is encoded, so nothing is sent and nothing is dropped. Muted, silent and the-network-died are indistinguishable from absence alone - read the mute-transitions panel. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Send Path - Datagrams Sent

panels.description: Frames the send path discarded, by a bounded send-drop vocabulary that is DISTINCT from the receive reject taxonomy. Every spelling EXCEPT `not_connected` deliberately matches MH's MediaDropReason, so `sum by(reason)` compares across the two ends of one hop; `not_connected` is client-only, because MH never initiates. The roster's one home is `MEDIA_SEND_DROP_REASONS` in `packages/sdk-core/src/media/setup/mediaMetrics.ts`, which a `toEqual` test pins - the correspondence is stated here by naming the exception, never by a count, so it cannot go stale on a sixth token. transport_send_refused and not_connected should both READ ZERO FOREVER. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS. The export pipeline is LIVE, so empty can mean no drops occurred, no browser has reported within the collector's metric_expiration, or the pipeline broke - run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MH MEDIA-PATH BOARD, where the drop panels read a flat ZERO when healthy (those counters are present-at-zero from startup; an ABSENT series there is a fault). Client series are created lazily on first emission, so here absence and zero are different states; do not carry the MH reading across. No client reject reason is video-gated - every token that can appear on this counter is reachable in this story. Stated explicitly because the equivalent MH drop panels DO name two reasons that cannot fire until video, and silence here would be indistinguishable from having forgotten to check. There is deliberately no 'or vector(0)' in this query: it would fabricate a series and flatten the by-reason breakdown that triage depends on.
panels.title: Send Path - Send Drops by Reason

panels.description: Depth of the DEEPEST of the sender's bounded egress lanes (one per target handler, each bounded independently), in frames. A full gauge with healthy frames_sent means ONE lane (one handler's path) is stalled, not the sender. Read against the configured bound - `media.egress.maxQueueFrames` and `media.audio.frameDurationMs` in `packages/sdk-core/src/config/clientConfig.ts` - their product is the lane's bound in time. Read the keys, not a figure copied here: a number on a board outlives the config it was copied from. The application bound trips BEFORE the transport high-water mark - asserted at setup - so a rising depth here is back-pressure we can count rather than loss inside the user agent. NOT an egress budget, capacity or ceiling: no such gauge exists in this story. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Send Path - Egress Queue Depth

panels.description: KEK arrivals through the KEK-source seam by source, and client mute transitions by action. Neither carries key material or a KEK generation - the generation is monotonic over a meeting's life, so as a label its cardinality is unbounded over TIME and a per-meeting generation series would be a membership-change trace. Client mute is enforced at CAPTURE and does not depend on the server honouring it. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Key and Mute Lifecycle

panels.description: Wall-clock milliseconds from media pipeline start to the first media frame arriving at the wire. Despite the name's resemblance to dt_client_time_to_first_mh_connected_ms this is NOT a frozen-roster member and carries the media-path label set, not the join-flow one - it has no meeting dimension of any kind. No objective attaches to it in this story. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Time to First Media Frame (p95 / p50)

panels.description: dt_client_media_capture_source{mode}: what feeds each client's send path, as a presence gauge (value 1 for the ACTIVE mode only; a microphone build never writes a test_tone series). THE VALUE IS NOT A BROWSER COUNT. Every browser sets 1 for its mode with no per-browser label (a per-session identity is barred by ADR-0036 §11), so all browsers in a mode write ONE series and the collector's view is last-writer-wins: sum by(mode) reads 1 whether one browser or a thousand carry that mode. Never read a level, a rise or a fall off this panel. THE ONLY SIGNAL IS THE PRESENCE OF THE mode="test_tone" SERIES (count(dt_client_media_capture_source{mode="test_tone"}) > 0). A test_tone series in any environment other than dev/test means a test-tone build (the Vite build-time define __DT_TEST_TONE__, story 2 R-7) is serving real users whose microphones are not being sent at all. Presence is judged over the lookback window, not per scrape: the SDK re-sets the gauge once per export interval on its own timer. No alert, deliberately - dev and test legitimately carry test_tone and the environment is not on the series. See docs/observability/metrics/client.md.
panels.title: Send Path - Capture Source (SAFETY: test_tone outside dev)

panels.description: dt_client_media_receive_source_deficit_total, unit assignment-intervals: per export interval, the number of ACTIVE receive assignments (MC assigned a sender and did not mark it source-muted) from which the client decoded NO frame for the whole interval. Observed decode activity is the receiver's ground truth; a rising line means MC claims a live source and nothing decodes. Plotted as increase(): silent assignment-intervals per step. rate(...) multiplied by the SDK's metric export interval (config key telemetry.metricExportIntervalMs, deliberately not restated here) is the mean number of silent active assignments fleet-wide. Premise: DTX is off, so a live sender always produces frames. BLIND to a declaration MC rejected whole (no active assignments) - see the Receive-Slot Refusals panel. Triage: docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md.
panels.title: Receive Path - Silent Active Sources (deficit)

panels.description: dt_client_media_receive_slots_rejected_total: startMedia() calls the SDK refused because the client's declared receive-slot count N (VITE_DT_RECEIVE_SLOTS) exceeds the cap MC advertised on JoinResponse.max_receive_slots (MC_MAX_RECEIVE_SLOTS). MC would reject the whole declaration, so the client refuses loudly and receives nothing. Reads zero on a correctly configured deployment. The deficit panel stays at 0 for this failure - this panel is its only signal. With an MC that predates the field, the same failure counts on MC's mc_media_receive_capability_declarations_total{outcome="slot_count_over_cap"} instead. Triage: docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md.
panels.title: Receive Path - Receive-Slot Refusals (N over MC cap)

panels.description: dt_client_media_kek_retention_violations_total - ALERTED by ClientKekRetentionViolation (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/client-alerts.yaml). A ZERO-FOREVER TRIPWIRE AGAINST A FUTURE REFACTOR, not a detector for a live condition: the retention invariant is held by a unit test, and the only known cause of a non-zero value is an SDK regression that retains more than one previous KEK generation (a COUNT bound, current plus ONE previous generation, not the W-derived time bound). RetentionGuard FAILS SAFE: it zeroizes and drops the excess in the same call, so no superseded key was kept. What is broken is the key-lifetime code that should have made the guard unnecessary. Remedy: roll back the web-app/SDK release; nothing MC-side helps, and changing MC_KEK_ROTATION_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS does not. SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. PRESENTED AS THE RAW SUMMED VALUE, NOT increase(): increase()/rate() need a prior sample and never see that first event, and for a tripwire the first event is the only one that matters - the alert reads the same presence form. No series is the healthy reading, but empty is equally what a broken pipeline looks like, so run the READ FIRST discriminator before trusting it. The value is the collector's accumulated count, and the series vanishes when the collector's metric_expiration (infra/services/otel-collector/collector.yaml) drops it idle - a vanished series is not a resolved one, and the alert clears then, not when the condition stops. Triage: docs/runbooks/mc-incident-response.md#tripwire-kek-retention-violation. # guard:ignore(lazy delta client tripwire counter first appears already at one so increase never sees the first event)
panels.title: Key Tripwire - KEK Retention Violations (ALERTED)

panels.description: dt_client_media_kek_install_refusals_total{outcome="conflicting_key"} - ALERTED by MCClientKekConflictingKey (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml). A client was handed DIFFERENT KEK bytes under a generation it already holds, and kept the held key. THIS IS THE SOLE OBSERVABLE WITNESS OF THAT ARM: the receive-side twin is unwrap_failed on peers, diluted inside MCMediaMissingKeyMaterial's fleet-wide ratio, so a small population is visible only here. Causes and what is NOT a cause are listed on the rule. The other two refusal arms are panel-only, on KEK Install Refusals below. SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. PRESENTED AS THE RAW SUMMED VALUE, NOT increase(): increase()/rate() need a prior sample and never see that first event, and for a tripwire the first event is the only one that matters - the alert reads the same presence form. No series is the healthy reading, but empty is equally what a broken pipeline looks like, so run the READ FIRST discriminator before trusting it. The value is the collector's accumulated count, and the series vanishes when the collector's metric_expiration (infra/services/otel-collector/collector.yaml) drops it idle - a vanished series is not a resolved one, and the alert clears then, not when the condition stops. Triage: docs/runbooks/mc-incident-response.md#tripwire-conflicting-kek. # guard:ignore(lazy delta client tripwire counter first appears already at one so increase never sees the first event)
panels.title: Key Tripwire - Conflicting KEK Refusals (ALERTED)

panels.description: dt_client_media_roster_key_rebinds_total. Target A is the rebind arm as its raw summed value (presence, the same form its alert reads); target B is the downgrade arm with increase() per ADR-0029, because downgrade is expected non-zero and its raw value is a collector-memory-bound accumulation that resets on expiry or restart. ONLY THE rebind ARM ALERTS, via MCClientRosterKeyRebind (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml): a live sender id bound to DIFFERENT, well-formed key bytes. Near-zero, NOT zero-forever - three causes: an MC roster-publication defect, a cache-poisoning attempt, or a lost ParticipantLeft followed by a sender-id reissue (that cause REQUIRES a sender-id-exhaustion epoch reset in the meeting - mc_meeting_kek_generated_total{trigger="sender_space_exhausted"} - and no reset rules it out; mc_participant_outbound_messages_dropped_total{payload_kind="participant_update_left"} over MC's lifetime only supports it, and a short-window zero rules nothing out). downgrade IS EXPECTED NON-ZERO and is never an alert input: MC publishing an empty key is a documented occurrence (see no_roster_entry). One increment per EVENT, not per purged key; no sender dimension. SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. THE rebind ARM IS PRESENTED AS THE RAW SUMMED VALUE, NOT increase(): increase()/rate() need a prior sample and never see that first event, and for a tripwire the first event is the only one that matters - the alert reads the same presence form. No series is the healthy reading, but empty is equally what a broken pipeline looks like, so run the READ FIRST discriminator before trusting it. The value is the collector's accumulated count, and the series vanishes when the collector's metric_expiration (infra/services/otel-collector/collector.yaml) drops it idle - a vanished series is not a resolved one, and the alert clears then, not when the condition stops. Triage: docs/runbooks/mc-incident-response.md#tripwire-roster-key-rebind. # guard:ignore(lazy delta client tripwire counter first appears already at one so increase never sees the first event)
panels.title: Roster Key Changes by Outcome (rebind ALERTED)

panels.description: dt_client_media_kek_retention_anomalies_total by outcome: a KEK message's W (the kek_rotation_debounce_seconds wire field, MC_KEK_ROTATION_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS, published by MC as mc_meeting_kek_rotation_window_seconds) produced a non-nominal retention window, min(W/2, KEK_RETENTION_CEILING_MS) derived by deriveKekRetention in packages/sdk-core/src/config/clientConfig.ts. One per KEK message; the denominator is dt_client_media_kek_updates_total. PANEL ONLY. floor_substituted AND ceiling_clamped ARE EXPECTED-NON-ZERO CONFIGURATION / ROLLBACK STATES AND ARE NEVER ALERT INPUTS. floor_substituted: W was zero or absent, i.e. an MC older than the kek_rotation_debounce_seconds field, so the client used KEK_RETENTION_FLOOR_MS - expected, fleet-wide, during a deliberate one-version MC rollback (the supported path, not an incident; do not roll further back). It is the fleet's only cluster-visible rollback detector. ceiling_clamped: W/2 exceeded KEK_RETENTION_CEILING_MS and retention was clamped. The shipped default W ALREADY sits at that ceiling, so raising MC_KEK_ROTATION_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS at all flips the whole fleet to a permanently climbing ceiling_clamped that changes retention by nothing and is NOT a fault - it is where an operator meets the fact that W is no longer the binding parameter. below_rewrap_latency: the derived retention does not exceed the client's transmit-key re-wrap latency, so frames wrapped under the previous generation can outlive it at the receiver; the client validates its floor at startup, so this fires only when MC's W/2 is too small - the remedy is in MC (raise MC_KEK_ROTATION_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS), never client-side. SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. Plotted with increase() per ADR-0029, so the FIRST increment of each series is invisible here (no prior sample); a series that exists at all has seen at least one event - check its presence in Explore if a single occurrence matters. Empty is ambiguous: run the READ FIRST discriminator.
panels.title: KEK Retention Anomalies by Outcome (never alerted)

panels.description: dt_client_media_kek_install_refusals_total, the two arms that do NOT alert: older_generation (a generation below the current; the holder never rolls back) and malformed (wrong width, all-zero, or a generation outside the wire's u16 range; refused and scrubbed). conflicting_key is excluded here - it alerts, and has its own tripwire panel above. Every refusal leaves the held state unchanged and working. Both arms read zero from an honest MC today (the client has no reconnect, so no holder outlives the KEK epoch it was given); an increment is a defect - an MC bug, or a client holding one KEK holder across two sessions - not a delivery hiccup. See docs/observability/metrics/client.md. (already_held is not a refusal: it is a wrap outcome, deliberately uncounted.) SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. Plotted with increase() per ADR-0029, so the FIRST increment of each series is invisible here (no prior sample); a series that exists at all has seen at least one event - check its presence in Explore if a single occurrence matters. Empty is ambiguous: run the READ FIRST discriminator.
panels.title: KEK Install Refusals - older_generation / malformed (panel only)

panels.description: dt_client_media_decode_queue_dropped_total: frames evicted from a per-sender decode lane's bounded pending queue while that lane's decoder is being created or replaced (overflow drops the oldest); one increment per evicted frame. PANEL ONLY. POST-ACCEPT: every frame counted here was already counted on dt_client_media_frames_accepted_total, so it sits DOWNSTREAM of received = accepted + sum(drops by reason), in the accepted-to-audible segment. It is NEVER a frames_dropped_total reason and is NEVER subtracted in that identity - folding it in would put one frame on both sides and break the identity silently, in aggregate. It exists because a queue eviction fires no decoder error callback, so Downlink Continuity and Decode's decoder-errors series does not see this loss. SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. Plotted with increase() per ADR-0029, so the FIRST increment of each series is invisible here (no prior sample); a series that exists at all has seen at least one event - check its presence in Explore if a single occurrence matters. Empty is ambiguous: run the READ FIRST discriminator.
panels.title: Receive Path - Decode Queue Drops (post-accept)

panels.description: increase(dt_client_media_kek_generations_retained_total) read AGAINST increase(dt_client_media_kek_updates_total{source="kek_update"}). PANEL ONLY. KEK UPDATES RISING WHILE RETENTIONS STAY FLAT IS THE SIGNAL: rotations are arriving and no install is keeping the previous generation, so every rotation costs an audio gap (the opposite failure from the retention-violation tripwire, which watches for retaining too MANY). NEITHER SERIES ALONE SAYS ANYTHING. kek_update is rotation pushes only (a reconnect re-issue rides the JoinResponse-shaped reconnect result and counts as join_response), and each push delivers a newer generation and demotes the current one, so the HEALTHY EXPECTATION IS ROUGHLY ONE-TO-ONE, less refusals (KEK Install Refusals and the conflicting-KEK tripwire panels). The divergence is the signal; flat retentions with flat updates is simply no rotation. Both count per browser. SERIES-ABSENT SEMANTICS: this counter is created lazily - the SDK exports DELTA and a counter only in an interval where it was recorded, so the series is ABSENT until the first increment and first appears in Prometheus already at >= 1. Plotted with increase() per ADR-0029, so the FIRST increment of each series is invisible here (no prior sample); a series that exists at all has seen at least one event - check its presence in Explore if a single occurrence matters. Empty is ambiguous: run the READ FIRST discriminator.
panels.title: KEK Rotations vs Generations Retained

title: Client SDK - Media Path
